items.followUp: Explain the formation of a double covalent bond in an oxygen molecule.

rubric.why: A covalent bond is based on the mutual sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms mutually share one or more pairs of electrons.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond consists of one shared pair of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that one pair of electrons is shared.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond consists of two shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that two pairs of electrons are shared.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that three pairs of electrons are shared.

rubric.why: These examples correspond to single, double, and triple covalent bonds, respectively.
rubric.description: Gives examples of the three covalent bond types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving H₂, O₂, and N₂ as examples of single, double, and triple bonds, respectively.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when atoms mutually share one or more pairs of electrons.
A single covalent bond is formed by sharing one pair of electrons; for example, H₂.
A double covalent bond is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons; for example, O₂.
A triple covalent bond is formed by sharing three pairs of electrons; for example, N₂.

items.followUp: Define chemical properties and give one example.

rubric.why: Physical properties are characteristics that can be determined by observation or measurement.
rubric.description: Identifies physical properties as observable or measurable characteristics of a substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing them as characteristics, or stating that they can be observed or measured.

rubric.why: A physical property can be determined without changing the substance's chemical composition.
rubric.description: States that determining a physical property does not change the substance chemically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea that the chemical composition remains unchanged.

modelAnswer: Physical properties are characteristics of a substance that can be observed or measured without changing its chemical composition.

items.followUp: State the number of electrons in the stable outer shell represented by the duplet and octet rules.

rubric.why: The duplet rule describes stability with two electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.description: States the stable outer-shell arrangement in the duplet rule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the duplet as a stable arrangement of two outermost-shell electrons.

rubric.why: The octet rule describes stability with eight electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.description: States the stable outer-shell arrangement in the octet rule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the octet as a stable arrangement of eight outermost-shell electrons.

modelAnswer: According to the duplet rule, an atom becomes stable when its outermost shell contains two electrons.
According to the octet rule, an atom becomes stable when its outermost shell contains eight electrons.
